subject: pharmacology
title: Warfarin, Vitamin K and INR Monitoring

steps.tx: **Warfarin** blocks vitamin K epoxide reductase (VKORC1), halting regeneration of reduced vitamin K and therefore gamma carboxylation of factors II, VII, IX and X and proteins C and S. Without carboxylation the liver secretes inert precursors. Onset waits for circulating factor II to decay (half life near 60 hours), so full anticoagulation takes four to five days despite an INR that rises early on factor VII's six hour half life, which is why heparin bridging overlaps initiation.
steps.say: Warfarin starves new clotting factors of vitamin K; the INR rises early but real protection waits for factor two to fall.

vis.alt: Warfarin mechanism illustration showing vitamin K cycle blockade and clotting factor depletion
vis.caption: Warfarin blocking the vitamin K cycle, depleting carboxylated factors II, VII, IX and X. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.tx: The **INR** (international normalised ratio) standardises the prothrombin time across reagents so a result of 2.5 means the same anticoagulation anywhere. Targets are indication specific: 2.0 to 3.0 for atrial fibrillation and venous thromboembolism, 2.5 to 3.5 for most mechanical heart valves with the mitral position and older designs at the higher band. Time in therapeutic range, not any single reading, predicts both clotting and bleeding outcomes.
steps.say: INR two to three for most, higher for mechanical mitral valves; time in range is the quality measure.

left.title: INR target bands
points: 2.0 to 3.0: atrial fibrillation and venous thromboembolism
2.5 to 3.5: mechanical mitral and older valves
Below range: clotting risk returns
Above 4.5: bleeding risk climbs steeply

right.title: Reading quality
points: Time in therapeutic range summarises control
Single readings mislead without trend
Point of care testing enables self management
Illness and diet changes demand earlier rechecks

steps.tx: **Genetics** writes the starting dose: CYP2C9 variants slow S warfarin clearance and VKORC1 variants change enzyme sensitivity, together explaining several fold dose differences between patients, with requirements from under 1 mg to over 10 mg daily. Algorithms combining genotype, age, body size, amiodarone and indication outperform fixed dosing in trials, yet clinical variables alone serve most services; either way, small increments and frequent early INR checks replace guesswork.
steps.say: Two genes and the drug list set the dose; titrate in small steps with frequent early INR checks.

nodes.label: Start 5 mg daily (lower if elderly, liver disease, interacting drugs)
INR checked from day 3 to 5 and titrated
Stable dose found, interval stretches to 4 to 12 weeks
Any new drug, diet or illness restarts close surveillance

steps.tx: Warfarin's interaction web is pharmacology's densest: CYP2C9 inhibitors (metronidazole, co trimoxazole, amiodarone, azoles) raise INR, enzyme inducers (rifampicin, carbamazepine, St John's wort) lower it, antibiotics also starve gut vitamin K production, and highly protein bound rivals displace it transiently. Alcohol, liver disease and thyrotoxicosis sensitise; **vitamin K** rich diets and supplements antagonise. Every medication change in a warfarin patient is an INR appointment, a rule with no exceptions worth memorising.
steps.say: Any new drug, antibiotic course or diet swing earns an INR check; warfarin forgives nothing silently.

left.title: INR climbers
points: Metronidazole, co trimoxazole, azole antifungals
Amiodarone (dose cut needed on starting)
Antibiotics reducing gut vitamin K synthesis
Alcohol excess and deteriorating liver function

right.title: INR fallers
points: Rifampicin and carbamazepine induction
St John's wort self medication
Vitamin K supplements and enteral feeds
Improved diet after illness related starvation

steps.tx: For supratherapeutic INR without bleeding, management is omission plus **vitamin K** judged by number and bleeding risk: hold warfarin, give oral vitamin K 1 to 2.5 mg when INR exceeds 10 or bleeding risk is high, and simply withhold for lesser elevations. Intravenous vitamin K works over 6 to 12 hours, oral over 24, so neither rescues active haemorrhage, where four factor prothrombin complex concentrate supplies the missing factors immediately alongside intravenous vitamin K for durability.
steps.say: High INR without bleeding: hold and consider oral vitamin K. Bleeding now: concentrate first, vitamin K for durability.

nodes.label: Hold warfarin, review causes and interacting drugs
Oral vitamin K if INR over 10 or bleeding risk high
Recheck INR in 24 to 48 hours, resume lower

steps.tx: Major bleeding on warfarin inverts the initiation choreography at speed: hold the drug, give four factor **prothrombin complex concentrate** dosed by INR and weight, add intravenous vitamin K 5 to 10 mg so hepatic synthesis resumes as the concentrate decays, and recheck INR within the hour. Fresh frozen plasma is the slower, volume heavy ancestor where concentrate is unavailable. Reversal is then a bridge to source control, endoscopy, surgery or embolisation as anatomy dictates.
steps.say: Concentrate replaces factors in minutes, vitamin K keeps them replaced; then find and fix the bleeding source.

left.title: Four factor PCC
points: Factors II, VII, IX, X in small volume
INR correction within minutes of infusion
Dose banded by presenting INR and weight
Preferred agent for warfarin major bleeding

right.title: Adjuncts and follow through
points: Intravenous vitamin K 5 to 10 mg for durability
Recheck INR and haemoglobin after reversal
Fresh frozen plasma only where PCC unavailable
Source control: endoscopy, surgery or embolisation

steps.tx: Because proteins C and S fall faster than factor II at initiation, **warfarin** briefly creates a prothrombotic imbalance before it anticoagulates, the mechanism behind warfarin skin necrosis in the next lesson and behind bridging heparin for acute thrombosis. Loading doses do not shorten the wait for factor II decay and only deepen the protein C trough, so modern practice starts modestly and bridges deliberately rather than front loading heroically.
steps.say: Protein C falls first, so warfarin can clot before it protects; bridge acute thrombosis and skip loading heroics.

nodes.label: Protein C (half life hours) falls before factor II (days)
Therapeutic heparin bridges until INR therapeutic two days

steps.tx: Warfarin crosses the placenta and is **teratogenic**, classically nasal hypoplasia and stippled epiphyses with first trimester exposure and fetal intracranial bleeding later, so mechanical valve pregnancies become specialist shared care balancing maternal valve thrombosis against fetal harm with heparins and dose adjusted warfarin in defined windows. Outside pregnancy its remaining fortresses are mechanical valves and antiphospholipid syndrome, where direct oral anticoagulants proved inferior or harmful in trials.
steps.say: Valves and antiphospholipid syndrome keep warfarin employed; pregnancy makes every week a specialist decision.

left.title: Warfarin strongholds
points: Mechanical heart valves, all positions
Moderate to severe rheumatic mitral stenosis with AF
Triple positive antiphospholipid syndrome
Severe renal failure where DOACs are untested

right.title: Pregnancy hazards
points: Embryopathy: nasal hypoplasia, stippled epiphyses
Fetal intracranial haemorrhage in later trimesters
Heparins substitute in defined windows
Mechanical valve pregnancy: specialist shared care
